findings.summary: The analyzer-ID band scheme shipped in rule-phase.js is recorded as an approved decision, but neither quote cited under `analyzer-id-record-and-bands` approves it — one is a directive naming no mechanism, the other is a clarification question that describes a different (global, not per-band) mechanism.
findings.evidence:
Live code — `.agents/workflows/rule-phase.js:1291`: "IDs run in bands: AG00xx for architecture rules, AG01xx for native-interop rules, AGSxxxx for the security band. Take the highest ID ever used inside that band and add one."

Contract `.dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/contract.md:266` records the same as decided, and the ONLY approving words cited (contract.md:270-278) are:
(a) "STOP THIS ... I can change the contract right now STOP dodging work by holding strict to the contract.\n\nNOW WHAT is the \"right\" solution?\n\nAND WE FIX IT NOW!" — a demand to fix, naming no mechanism and no bands.
(b) "ARe you basically just saying keep a ledger of reused ones and if it is not in that leger use greatest plus one?" — a question, and it states ONE global "greatest plus one", with no band partition anywhere in it.

The difference is material and developer-visible. Against the live release file `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md` (AG0001–AG0039, AG0101–AG0116, AGS5443), Tim's global "greatest plus one" yields AG0117 for a new architecture rule; the shipped per-band rule yields AG0040. Two different permanent identifiers from the same instruction.

An \"approval\" that is really a non-answer, a topic change, or a reword / clarify request treated as a yes." `.agents/skills/rails-decisions/SKILL.md:46` — "Violation — paraphrased decision. A recorded decision whose text does not match, verbatim, what Tim approved."
